title: Compiled conditions decide their truth
statement: Let $S$ be a setting, and suppose a start configuration for a statement $s$ at depth $d$, code position $\mathrm{pos}$, and stack position $q$ satisfies the start conditions, with word-RAM memory $m$. Let $c$ be a condition whose compiled code occurs at $\mathrm{pos}$, whose width is at most $S.F$, and which is safe for a light state $\sigma$ under the limits of $S$. Then there exist a word-RAM memory $m'$ and a natural number $k\le\mathrm{size}(c)$ such that $m'$ agrees with $m$ outside the scratch-address set for frame size $S.F$; if $c$ holds in $\sigma$, the compiled code takes $k$ steps from position $\mathrm{pos}$ to $\mathrm{pos}+\mathrm{size}(c)$, and if $c$ does not hold, it takes $k$ steps from $\mathrm{pos}$ to branch position $l$.
hypotheses_covered: A start configuration for $s$ at depth $d$, position $\mathrm{pos}$, and stack position $q$, with memory $m$
The compiled condition code for $c$ occurs at $\mathrm{pos}$
replaced:
Let $S$ be a setting and suppose a start configuration for a statement $s$ at depth $d$,
code position $\mathrm{pos}$, and stack position $q$ has word-RAM memory $m$. Let $c$ be
a condition whose compiled code occurs at $\mathrm{pos}$, whose width is at most $S.F$,
and which is safe for the light state $\sigma$ under limits $S.\mathrm{lim}$. Then there
are a memory $m'$ and a natural number $n$ with $n\le \mathrm{size}(c)$ such that $m'$
agrees with $m$ outside the scratch locations (the designated condition registers and
temporary registers); if $c$ holds in $\sigma$, the compiled condition takes $n$ steps
from position $\mathrm{pos}$ to $\mathrm{pos}+\mathrm{size}(c)$, and if $c$ does not
hold, it takes $n$ steps from position $\mathrm{pos}$ to the specified branch position
$l$.
